_readme: Persistent fetch-failure ledger for the Las Azules S2 media sweep routine. Sweeps must read this before attempting any body fetch on a candidate URL and skip anything currently in cooldown, rendering the skip on the sweep evidence line. failCount tracks consecutive full fallback-chain failures (WebFetch AND Firecrawl scrape both failed in the same attempt). Three consecutive full-chain failures sets cooldownUntil to 30 days out. After cooldown expires, the URL gets one retry (WebFetch then Firecrawl); success resets failCount to 0 and clears cooldownUntil, failure restarts the 30-day cooldown. A separate category, permanentSkip with a skipReason, marks URLs that are fetchable but excluded for an editorial reason (for example a syndicated republication of a story already in data.json under a primary outlet). permanentSkip entries are skipped regardless of cooldownUntil and must never be treated as, or logged as, a fetch failure. See LEMA-9620 for origin, LEMA-9619 for the incident that motivated this file, and LEMA-9621 for the permanentSkip category. Two standing editorial rules, adopted LEMA-9642 (CEO ruling on LEMA-9641), apply to every sweep going forward and must not be re-escalated: (1) No proxy, inferred, or approximated dates ever enter data.json. A crawler artifact like this ledger's firstSeen timestamp is never a substitute for a real, sourced publish date -- not even with a disclaimer in the excerpt, because sorting and the dashboard KPIs read ts, not the excerpt. If no real publish date can be recovered (WebFetch AND Firecrawl both exhausted), the candidate is permanentSkip with skipReason "editorial_undateable" and reviewable: true, never added with a substitute date. (2) Social-candidate relevance gate, separate from and prior to any dateability check: vendor, supplier, crew-personal, and fan-repost accounts are not media coverage and must be skipped as permanentSkip on relevance grounds (skipReason "editorial_vendor_promo" for a vendor/supplier company account, "editorial_personal_repost" for an individual crew-personal or fan-repost account) regardless of whether a date could be found. Publisher, outlet, and editorial-brand accounts are media coverage and are evaluated normally, dateability included. reviewable: true (used on editorial_undateable entries only) marks a permanentSkip entry as genuine coverage omitted solely for lack of a real date, distinct from editorial_redundant_syndication (we already have the story) and editorial_vendor_promo/editorial_personal_repost (not coverage at all, dateability irrelevant). It is queryable only, for a future manual date lookup; it implies no dashboard or UI surfacing. A third standing rule, adopted 2026-09-06 (CEO ruling on LEMA-9761, implemented in LEMA-9762), applies going forward and must not be re-escalated: (3) no un-ledgered exclusions. Any decision to exclude a candidate from data.json must be written to this ledger as a permanentSkip entry in the same run the decision is made; a decision recorded only in a run comment or deliverable document does not persist, because the next sweep cannot see it. An exclusion must use one of the existing skipReason values above. Agents must not invent a new exclusion ground mid-run: if no existing skipReason fits a candidate, the candidate is included in data.json that run and a new issue is opened escalating the proposed category, rather than being excluded on an invented ground. Two scope clarifications travel with this rule: first-party promotional and BTS video produced by the studio or platform itself (trailers, "inside look" pieces, cast interview clips, press releases, official show pages) is media coverage under Rule B like any other official show/network account content, evaluated normally for dateability and duplication, not a candidate for a new editorial skip category. There is no publish-date floor on candidates: coverage is never excluded, under any rule, on the grounds that it predates Season 2, and Season 1 era coverage is in scope on the same terms as Season 2 coverage. A fourth standing rule, adopted 2026-09-10 (CEO ruling on LEMA-9880, implemented in LEMA-9883), applies going forward and must not be re-escalated: (4) Rule A applies retroactively, plus two guardrails. Rule A governs what ts means, not when an entry was written or which sweep run committed it: an entry that violates Rule A today violates it regardless of vintage, and there is no grandfathering for entries already in data.json. Rule C does not block retroactive remediation: Rule C governs how an exclusion is recorded (ledgered, in the run where the decision is made, using an existing skipReason), not when the candidate was first seen. A retroactive removal of an already-published entry satisfies Rule C when the data.json removal and the matching fetch-blocklist.json permanentSkip entry land in the same commit, because the remediation run is the run where the decision is made. Guardrail one, ledger precedence: before writing any permanentSkip entry to this ledger, check whether that same URL is already present in data.json. If it is, this ledger wins: remove the data.json entry in the same commit that adds the permanentSkip entry, rather than leaving a live feed entry that a permanentSkip entry silently contradicts. Guardrail two, future-ts guard: any candidate or existing data.json entry whose ts is later than the sweep's run date is an automatic Rule A violation, a publish date cannot be in the future, and must never be committed; an existing entry found with a future ts must be flagged and remediated under this rule (removed and ledgered in the same commit), not left in place.
